# Cheapest Way to Accept International Card Payments as an Indian SaaS Business in 2026: A Guide for Billing USA, UK, and Global Customers


September 28, 2026


[Shashank Yadav](https://salarybox.in/blog/author/shashank87cc9f270b/)


[No comments yet](https://salarybox.in/blog/cheapest-way-to-accept-international-card-payments-as-an-indian-saas-business-in-2026-a-guide-for-billing-usa-uk-and-global-customers/#respond)


A SaaS founder in Pune was billing $8,000 MRR from US and UK clients. His international payment gateway dashboard showed a transaction fee of 4.4%. What it did not show was the 3.5% foreign exchange conversion markup applied before a single dollar reached his account. The real cost was closer to 8% per dollar billed. At $8,000 MRR, that difference cost approximately Rs. 4.25 lakh per year in fees alone, separate from a weekly FIRA batch that turned GST refund reconciliation into a monthly accounting exercise.


The cheapest international payment gateway for an Indian SaaS business is not the one with the lowest advertised transaction fee. It is the one with the lowest combined cost of transaction fee, FX markup, and failed subscription recovery — backed by a full RBI PA-CB licence that keeps banking relationships clean as billing volume scales.


This analysis compares five major international payment gateways available to Indian SaaS businesses in 2026, evaluated on the criteria that determine actual revenue retained, not the headline rate on a pricing page.


**Key Takeaways**
-The true cost of accepting international card payments has three components: transaction fee (visible), FX markup above mid-market rate (usually hidden), and failed renewal cost from low cross-border success rates (never shown on a pricing page). Most Indian SaaS businesses optimise only for the first.


-Razorpay International Payment Gateway is the only Indian payment aggregator with a published 95%+ cross-border success rate, achieved through smart routing across multiple acquiring banks.


-On a $5,000 MRR SaaS business, the difference between the lowest and highest cost international payment gateway in this comparison amounts to approximately Rs. 22,000 per month, or Rs. 2.6 lakh per year — purely from fee differences, before success rate impact is included.


-Stripe India has been invite-only since May 2024 with no confirmed relaunch timeline. Its all-in cost of approximately 6.3% is second-highest in this comparison.


-PayPal’s all-in effective cost reaches approximately 8.25% on each invoice once the FX conversion markup is included, making it the most expensive international payment gateway for Indian SaaS businesses in 2026.


-As of June 2026, only approximately 19-25 entities hold full RBI PA-CB licences. Using a payment gateway without one for cross-border aggregation carries regulatory and operational risk.


-Auto-eFIRC per transaction is mandatory for GST refund claims on software export revenue. Confirm this feature with any international payment gateway before onboarding, not after.


## **Evaluation Criteria for Indian SaaS Teams**


Selecting an international payment gateway for SaaS recurring billing requires different criteria than selecting one for e-commerce. The factors that determine actual revenue retained:


- **Transaction fee (the visible cost).**


Published as a percentage of each transaction. For international cards, this ranges from 3% to 8.25% all-in across the international payment gateways in this comparison.


- **FX markup (the hidden cost).**


The gap between the exchange rate a payment gateway applies and the mid-market rate. A payment gateway advertising 4.3% but applying a 2% FX spread costs 6.3% in total. This figure rarely appears on pricing pages and must be confirmed directly.


- **Payment success rate (the silent revenue leak)**


International card renewals fail at higher rates than domestic transactions, due to issuer-side fraud flags, 3DS re-authentication friction, and currency mismatch rejections. A payment gateway with a 95% cross-border success rate on a $5,000 MRR book recovers $250 more per month than one at a 90% success rate, before any fee comparison is made.


- **RBI PA-CB licence.**


The Payment Aggregator Cross-Border licence, introduced by the RBI in October 2023, governs which entities can legally aggregate cross-border payments in India. Payment gateways without it operate under legacy OPGSP arrangements, with lower transaction limits and less regulatory certainty.


- **Recurring billing and dunning support.**


SaaS businesses need subscription retry logic, intelligent dunning, and reliable webhook notifications for failed payments. Depth varies significantly across international payment gateways.


- **Auto-eFIRC per transaction.**


Electronic Foreign Inward Remittance Certificates are required for every inward remittance on export of services, and are the primary documentation for GST zero-rated export refund claims. Manual FIRA requests from a bank take 7 to 15 business days per batch.


## **The True Cost Framework for International SaaS Payments**


Most international payment gateway comparisons stop at the transaction fee. For SaaS businesses billing internationally, the complete formula is:


***Net INR Received = (MRR in USD x INR rate) – (MRR x transaction fee %) – (MRR x FX markup %)***


Worked example at $5,000 MRR (Rs. 85 per USD mid-market rate):


**Payment Gateway** **Fee %** **FX Markup** **Effective All-in Cost** **Est. INR Received on $5,000 MRR**


Gateway A 3% 0% 3% Rs. 4,12,250


Gateway B 4.3% 2% 6.3% Rs. 3,98,225


Gateway C 4.99% ~1.5% ~6.5% Rs. 3,97,375


Gateway D 4.4% + $0.30 3-4% ~8.25% Rs. 3,89,938


The fee-only comparison above does not capture the success rate dimension. A payment gateway with a 95% cross-border success rate recovers approximately Rs. 2.55 lakh more per year at $5,000 MRR than one operating at 90%, independently of fee levels. Razorpay publishes its cross-border success rate at 95%+. No other international payment gateway in this comparison has published an equivalent figure for India-based merchants.


**Watch out:** FX markup is almost never disclosed on a public pricing page. Before onboarding any international payment gateway, request the exact exchange rate applied on a live $1,000 test transaction and compare it against the mid-market rate on the same day. The difference, annualised over your MRR, is often larger than the transaction fee itself.


***Did You Know?*** *Indian software and IT services exports reached a record USD 421 billion in FY2025-26. The RBI’s PA-CB framework, introduced in October 2023, now governs which payment gateways can legally aggregate these cross-border inflows, replacing the older OPGSP framework under which hundreds of entities previously operated. As of mid-2026, approximately 19-25 entities hold full PA-CB licences.*


## **International Payment Gateway Reviews for Indian SaaS**


### **Rank 1. Razorpay International Payment Gateway**


**Parameter** **Value**


International card fee 3% + 18% GST


FX markup Mid-market rate positioning


Effective all-in cost ~3%


Cross-border success rate 95%+


PA-CB licence Full, inward + outward (Dec 2025)


Apple Pay Yes (first Indian payment aggregator, Sep 2025)


Recurring billing Yes, with subscription retry


Auto-eFIRC Yes, per transaction


Settlement T+2


[Razorpay International Payment Gateway](https://razorpay.com/international-payment-gateway-india/) holds a full RBI PA-CB licence granted December 2025, covering both inward and outward cross-border payments. It is the only Indian payment aggregator to publish a cross-border success rate (95%+), achieved through smart routing across multiple acquiring banks. On a $5,000 MRR book, that success rate differential versus unoptimised routing represents approximately $3,000 per year in additional recovered subscription revenue.


For SaaS recurring billing, Razorpay supports subscription management, automatic retry on failed renewals, and webhook-based dunning notifications. In September 2025, Razorpay became the first Indian payment aggregator to launch Apple Pay for international customers, a payment method with approximately 30-40% adoption among US and UK smartphone users. Pilot data showed a 58% lift in subscription conversion rates and a 45% faster checkout time.


Razorpay auto-generates eFIRC per transaction, removing the 7-to-15-business-day manual bank documentation process that most other international payment gateways leave to the merchant.


**Honest limitation:** The 3% card rate looks higher than some advertised rates at first glance. The comparison changes once FX markup from competing payment gateways is included. International EMI and Amex card rates differ from the standard 3% and should be confirmed during onboarding.


**Pros:**


- Only Indian payment aggregator with a published 95%+ cross-border success rate
- Full PA-CB licence covering both inward and outward flows
- Apple Pay and Google Pay for international subscribers (first mover in India)
- Auto-eFIRC per transaction for FEMA and GST refund compliance
- Subscription retry and dunning logic built into the payment gateway
- 135 currencies, 180+ countries
- No setup fee, no annual maintenance charge


**Cons:**


- 3% standard card rate is not the lowest advertised rate in the market
- Dashboard can feel feature-heavy for teams new to the Razorpay product surface
- International EMI and Amex transactions are priced at a different rate from the standard card fee


**Best for:** Indian SaaS businesses at all revenue stages billing US and UK customers on recurring international cards, where success rate, regulatory compliance, and FEMA documentation automation are primary requirements.


### **Rank 2. PayU International Payment Gateway**


**Parameter** **Value**


International card fee Custom (not publicly disclosed)


FX markup Not published


Effective all-in cost Not disclosed


Cross-border success rate 85%+


PA-CB licence Full, inward + outward (Nov 2025)


Apple Pay Not confirmed


Recurring billing Yes (via PayU Subscriptions)


Auto-eFIRC Not confirmed


Settlement T+2 to T+3


PayU is one of India’s largest payment gateways by domestic volume, handling over 40% of India’s online payment transactions. In November 2025, it received integrated RBI authorisation simultaneously as PA-Online, PA-Physical, and PA-Cross Border, giving it one of the most complete regulatory stacks in the market.


The international payment gateway product supports multi-currency pricing, Dynamic Currency Conversion, and subscription billing via PayU Subscriptions. For SaaS businesses already running domestic billing through PayU, extending to international card acceptance happens within the same API stack and merchant dashboard.


The primary evaluation difficulty is pricing opacity. PayU does not publish cross-border transaction fees. Rates are negotiated individually after document verification, making cost comparison before onboarding effectively impossible. No cross-border success rate has been published for India-based merchants.


**Pros:**


- Full PA-CB licence covering both inward and outward cross-border flows
- Largest domestic payment gateway infrastructure in India
- Single platform for domestic and international billing
- Multi-currency checkout for international subscribers
- PayU Subscriptions supports recurring international billing


**Cons:**


- No published cross-border pricing; cost comparison requires a sales conversation before onboarding
- No published cross-border success rate for India-based merchants
- T+2 to T+3 settlement is slower than leading international payment gateways
- Apple Pay support not confirmed
- Auto-eFIRC status not confirmed


**Best for:** Enterprise Indian SaaS businesses with existing PayU domestic payment gateway relationships looking to extend recurring billing to international subscribers under a single commercial arrangement.


***Did You Know?*** *Cross-border card renewals for SaaS subscriptions fail at 12-18% higher rates than domestic renewals, according to payment infrastructure benchmarks. A payment gateway with smart routing and automatic retry logic can recover a material share of that gap. At $10,000 MRR, a 5 percentage point improvement in cross-border renewal success rate is worth approximately $6,000 per year in recovered subscription revenue before any fee comparison.*


### **Rank 3. CCAvenue International Payment Gateway**


**Parameter** **Value**


International card fee Up to 4.99%


FX markup XE rates (~1-2% above mid-market)


Effective all-in cost ~5.5-6.5%


Cross-border success rate Not published


PA-CB licence No


Apple Pay Not confirmed


Recurring billing Limited international support


Auto-eFIRC Not confirmed


Settlement Not published for international


CCAvenue is one of India’s oldest payment gateways, with international card coverage across 200+ countries and 27-currency Dynamic Currency Conversion. For basic one-time international card acceptance, it provides broad coverage. For SaaS recurring billing in 2026, two structural issues apply.


First, CCAvenue’s parent entity, Infibeam Avenues, does not hold an RBI PA-CB licence as of June 2026. It holds PA-O and PA-P authorisations, but not PA-CB. Cross-border payments facilitated through this payment gateway operate under legacy OPGSP arrangements, outside the current regulatory framework governing cross-border payment aggregation in India.


Second, the effective all-in cost reaches 5.5-6.5% once the XE rate FX spread (typically 1-2% above mid-market) is added to the headline fee of up to 4.99%. This is among the highest in this comparison for card acceptance.


**Pros:**


- Long-established payment gateway with broad international card acceptance
- 200 countries, 27-currency Dynamic Currency Conversion
- 18-language checkout for international buyers
- PCI DSS Level 1 certified


**Cons:**


- No PA-CB licence as of mid-2026, operates outside current regulatory framework
- Effective all-in cost of 5.5-6.5% once FX markup is included
- No published cross-border success rate
- Limited recurring billing infrastructure for international SaaS use cases
- Auto-eFIRC status not confirmed


**Best for:** Indian businesses with legacy CCAvenue integrations needing basic international card acceptance and without immediate PA-CB compliance requirements.


### **Rank 4. Stripe India – Best API, Very Limited Access**


**Parameter** **Value**


International card fee ~4.3%


FX markup 2% above mid-market


Effective all-in cost ~6.3%


Cross-border success rate Not published for India-based merchants


PA-CB licence No (surrendered Jul 2024)


Apple Pay No (in Indian cross-border merchant context)


Recurring billing Yes (Stripe Billing, Revenue Recovery)


Auto-eFIRC No, manual bank request (7-15 business days)


Settlement Variable


Stripe has the strongest developer tooling in the international payment gateway category globally. Stripe Billing, Revenue Recovery (automated dunning), and Stripe Radar (fraud prevention) are the benchmark products for SaaS subscription infrastructure. For an Indian SaaS team with confirmed Stripe access and the engineering capacity to integrate, the product quality is genuine.


Two problems define Stripe India in 2026. Access has been invite-only since May 2024 with no confirmed general availability relaunch. The payment gateway surrendered its PA-CB licence in July 2024. Even for businesses that secure access, the all-in cost is approximately 6.3% (4.3% plus 2% FX markup), FIRA requires a manual request to the merchant’s own bank taking 7-15 business days, and Apple Pay is not available in the Indian cross-border merchant context.


**Pros:**


- Best-in-class developer API and Stripe Billing documentation in the international payment gateway category
- Stripe Revenue Recovery for automated failed subscription retry and dunning
- Stripe Radar for cross-border fraud prevention
- Native Shopify integration


**Cons:**


- Invite-only since May 2024, no confirmed access for most Indian businesses
- No PA-CB licence (surrendered July 2024)
- ~6.3% all-in cost, second-highest in this comparison
- No auto-FIRA; manual bank request takes 7-15 business days per batch
- No Apple Pay for Indian cross-border merchants
- No published cross-border success rate for India-based merchants


**Best for:** Indian SaaS businesses that have confirmed Stripe access and are willing to accept the 6.3% all-in cost and manual FIRA overhead in exchange for Stripe Billing’s subscription management product.


### **Rank 5. PayPal – Most Expensive International Payment Gateway for SaaS**


**Parameter** **Value**


Transaction fee 4.4% + USD 0.30 per transaction


FX markup 3-4% above mid-market


Effective all-in cost ~8.25%


Cross-border success rate Not published


PA-CB licence In-principle (export only, May 2025)


Apple Pay No


Recurring billing PayPal Subscriptions (limited India support)


Auto-eFIRC Weekly batch FIRA only (since Feb 2026)


Settlement INR auto-converted daily


PayPal’s effective all-in cost for Indian SaaS businesses reaches approximately 8.25% once the transaction fee, fixed per-transaction charge, and FX conversion markup are combined. At $5,000 MRR, the monthly fee cost is approximately Rs. 35,000, compared to approximately Rs. 12,750 for a payment gateway charging 3% at mid-market FX rates. The annualised difference is Rs. 2.67 lakh on $5,000 MRR alone.


For recurring SaaS billing, PayPal’s subscription infrastructure has material limitations for India-based merchants. Incoming USD auto-converts to INR daily, removing any ability to time conversion. The RBI PA-CB status remains in-principle only (export side), granted May 2025, with full authorisation still pending. FIRA is issued weekly as a consolidated batch, not per transaction, creating reconciliation work for per-invoice GST refund claims.


**Pros:**


- Widely recognised brand name that provides checkout trust with international clients
- Weekly FIRA batch now issued (since February 2026)


**Cons:**


- ~8.25% all-in effective cost, highest in this comparison
- Forced daily INR auto-conversion, no option to hold foreign currency
- In-principle PA-CB only (export side), full authorisation still pending
- Weekly FIRA batch complicates per-transaction GST reconciliation
- No Apple Pay or Google Pay for subscription checkout
- Limited recurring billing infrastructure for India-based SaaS merchants


**Best for:** One-off invoices from international clients who have an existing PayPal wallet and no alternative payment preference.

Over 70% of that revenue is expected to come from international customers, primarily in the United States, United Kingdom, and Australia. The international payment gateway a SaaS business selects now directly determines how much of each subscription dollar survives the journey from a US customer’s card to an Indian bank account.*

## **The Failed Renewal Problem: Why SaaS Teams Must Ask About Success Rates**


One cost that no international payment gateway pricing page discloses is the revenue lost to failed card renewals. For SaaS businesses, a failed renewal is not just a lost transaction. It is the start of an involuntary churn event that, without sufficient retry attempts and smart dunning logic, becomes a permanent subscriber loss.


Cross-border card renewals fail at higher rates than domestic transactions. International cards trigger issuer-side fraud flags on recurring charges from foreign entities. 3DS re-authentication requests reduce renewal completion rates for cards enrolled in strong authentication programs. Currency conversion rejections add a further failure mode that domestic billing does not face.


Razorpay’s 3% transaction fee on international cards is higher than some advertised rates. But its 95%+ published cross-border success rate, combined with smart routing across multiple acquiring banks, means a materially higher share of subscription charges actually complete. No other international payment gateway in this comparison has published an equivalent cross-border success figure for India-based merchants.


When requesting proposals from any international payment gateway, ask for this specific data point: cross-border card renewal success rate for Indian SaaS merchants, by card network and geography, over the past 12 months. The answer, or the inability to provide one, tells you most of what you need to know.


## **USA and UK: What Customers’ Payment Habits Mean for Subscription Billing**


**United States.** Visa and Mastercard dominate. Apple Pay has reached approximately 30% adoption among US smartphone users as of 2025 and is particularly high among B2C SaaS subscribers on mobile. American Express is material for B2B SaaS serving enterprise buyers. An international payment gateway without Apple Pay loses a growing segment of US subscribers at the signup stage.


**United Kingdom.** Apple Pay adoption in the UK is approximately 40% of card holders. Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) is enforced for recurring payments under UK FCA rules. A payment gateway with SCA-compatible 3DS handling is required for UK subscriber billing.


**Canada and Australia.** Card-dominant markets with growing Apple Pay penetration. No significant payment method differences requiring payment gateway-specific handling beyond standard card acceptance.


**UAE.** Card and Apple Pay. No exchange control complications for Indian software exporters.


## **Which International Payment Gateway Should Indian SaaS Teams Choose?**


- **Early-stage SaaS ($0-$10,000 MRR) billing US and UK customers:** Razorpay International Payment Gateway provides the most complete starting point. Full PA-CB licence, 95%+ cross-border success rate, Apple Pay for US and UK subscribers, auto-eFIRC per transaction, and a transparent 3% card fee with no hidden FX markup. Subscription retry logic and dunning support are included.


- **Mid-scale SaaS ($10,000-$50,000 MRR):** Razorpay’s 95%+ success rate delivers material recovered MRR at this volume. The success rate gap versus an unoptimised international payment gateway represents Rs. 5.1 lakh to Rs. 25.5 lakh per year in additional recovered subscription revenue at this MRR range (at a 5 percentage point success rate advantage). Auto-eFIRC automation becomes operationally significant at this billing volume for FEMA and GST compliance.


- **Enterprise SaaS with an existing PayU domestic payment gateway relationship:** PayU International is a reasonable extension of existing domestic billing infrastructure. The pricing opacity is a limitation for cost comparison, but for enterprise teams negotiating directly, PayU’s full PA-CB licence and scale make it a viable international payment gateway.


- **SaaS teams with confirmed Stripe access:** Stripe Billing and Revenue Recovery are the strongest recurring subscription management products in the international payment gateway category. If access is confirmed and the team accepts the 6.3% all-in cost and manual FIRA overhead, it is a functional choice. For businesses without confirmed access, it is not a practical option in 2026.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the cheapest international payment gateway for Indian SaaS businesses in 2026?**


On a total cost basis combining transaction fee and FX markup, Razorpay International Payment Gateway has the lowest all-in cost among the international payment gateways reviewed: approximately 3% with mid-market FX positioning. CCAvenue and Stripe reach 6.3-6.5% all-in once FX markup is included. PayPal reaches approximately 8.25%. PayU does not publish cross-border pricing. At $5,000 MRR, the annual difference between Razorpay and PayPal amounts to approximately Rs. 2.67 lakh in fees, before the success rate advantage is factored in.


### **How much does accepting international cards cost for an Indian SaaS business?**


Transaction fees range from 3% (Razorpay) to 8.25% all-in (PayPal) across the international payment gateways in this comparison. The variation comes primarily from FX markup, which is added above the advertised transaction fee by most payment gateways and is rarely disclosed on public pricing pages. At $5,000 MRR, the annual fee cost ranges from approximately Rs. 1.53 lakh (Razorpay) to Rs. 4.21 lakh (PayPal).


### **What is the RBI PA-CB licence and do Indian SaaS businesses need it?**


The PA-CB (Payment Aggregator – Cross Border) licence, introduced by the RBI in October 2023, governs which entities can legally aggregate cross-border payments in India. Payment gateways without it operate under legacy OPGSP arrangements with lower transaction limits and less regulatory certainty. As of June 2026, Razorpay and PayU hold full PA-CB licences. CCAvenue does not hold one. Stripe surrendered its licence in July 2024. PayPal holds in-principle approval only. For any SaaS business with recurring international billing, a PA-CB licensed international payment gateway is the appropriate choice for long-term regulatory security.


### **Does Razorpay support recurring international card payments for SaaS?**


Yes. Razorpay International Payment Gateway supports recurring card billing, subscription management, automatic retry on failed renewals, and webhook-based dunning notifications. It also supports Apple Pay and Google Pay at the subscription signup stage, with pilot data from September 2025 showing a 58% lift in subscription conversion rates. Auto-eFIRC is generated per transaction for FEMA and GST refund compliance.


### **Can Indian SaaS companies accept Apple Pay from US and UK subscribers?**


As of June 2026, Razorpay International Payment Gateway is the only Indian-licensed payment aggregator that supports Apple Pay for international customers. Apple Pay was launched in September 2025, with pilot data showing a 58% conversion lift and a 95% success rate across 5,000+ payments. No other international payment gateway in this comparison has confirmed Apple Pay availability for Indian cross-border merchants.


### **What is auto-eFIRC and which international payment gateways provide it?**


eFIRC (Electronic Foreign Inward Remittance Certificate) is the mandatory documentation for every inward remittance on export of services in India. It is required for GST refund claims under the zero-rated export rules that apply to software and SaaS exports. Auto-generation means the international payment gateway creates this certificate per transaction without the merchant requesting it manually. Razorpay generates eFIRC automatically per transaction. Stripe requires a manual bank request taking 7-15 business days per batch. PayPal issues a weekly consolidated FIRA. PayU’s auto-eFIRC status has not been publicly confirmed.


### **Is Stripe available for Indian SaaS businesses in 2026?**


Stripe has been invite-only in India since May 2024 and surrendered its PA-CB licence in July 2024. Access requires a direct application with no confirmed timeline for approval. Most Indian SaaS businesses, particularly early-stage and mid-scale teams, do not have and cannot obtain Stripe access. For those without access, Razorpay International Payment Gateway provides comparable card acquiring infrastructure with full PA-CB compliance and significantly lower all-in costs.


### **What is a typical cross-border card success rate for SaaS subscription renewals?**


Razorpay publishes its cross-border transaction success rate at 95%+, achieved through smart routing across multiple acquiring banks. This is the only published figure among the international payment gateways reviewed here for India-based merchants. Industry benchmarks for cross-border recurring card billing suggest average success rates in the 82-88% range without smart routing. At $5,000 MRR, a 5 percentage point success rate advantage translates to approximately $3,000 per year in additionally recovered subscription revenue, independently of any fee comparison.
